skill.name: when-configuring-sandbox-security-use-sandbox-configurator
skill.description: Configure sandbox security boundaries for Claude Code workflows, including file isolation, network controls, testing, and monitoring guidance.
skill.summary: Guides teams through sandbox security policy design, isolation setup, validation tests, and monitoring.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The skill has a legitimate defensive purpose, but it includes executable shell workflows that modify host security settings, firewall rules, and privileged system files. Several static findings are false positives because they are deny-list entries or documentation, but sensitive-file tests and privileged configuration commands remain real risks.

remediation.issue: Privileged host modification commands are presented as runnable examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit warnings to run only in disposable test environments, require manual approval, and provide rollback steps before changing /etc, AppArmor, iptables, or hosts files.

remediation.issue: Security tests attempt to read /etc/shadow and ~/.ssh/id_rsa.
remediation.suggestion: Replace live sensitive-file reads with mocked fixture paths or container-only test files that prove deny rules without touching real host secrets.

remediation.issue: The workflow executes npx claude-flow@alpha without pinning an immutable version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed version or remove npx hook calls from the marketplace skill instructions.

remediation.issue: Monitoring commands can collect sensitive audit and packet metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Document retention, access control, and scoping requirements before enabling audit-log tailing or tcpdump.

semantic_findings.title: Privileged Host Security Configuration Changes
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to write files under /etc/security and /etc/apparmor.d, load an AppArmor profile, modify /etc/hosts, and set iptables default policies. These commands can disrupt the host or network if run outside a disposable environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited sections directly modify privileged system configuration and firewall state. The intent is defensive, but the operational blast radius is high.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned External Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The workflow repeatedly invokes npx claude-flow@alpha hooks and memory commands. Using an alpha package through npx can execute remote package code during the workflow and increases supply-chain risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The content explicitly uses npx with an alpha package name in executable instructions. This is clear external code execution, even though no malicious intent is proven.

semantic_findings.title: Continuous Monitoring Commands May Capture Sensitive Activity
semantic_findings.description: The monitoring script tails audit logs and starts tcpdump on all interfaces. This can collect sensitive file-access and network metadata if enabled without retention limits and access controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script directly starts audit-log and packet monitoring commands. The risk depends on deployment controls, but the collection behavior is explicit.

content.value_statement: Sandboxed coding agents need clear file, network, and resource boundaries to reduce host exposure. This skill provides a structured workflow for defining policies, creating isolation scripts, testing controls, and documenting the security posture.
actual_capabilities: Documents sandbox security requirements and threat models.
Defines file system allow lists, deny lists, and temporary workspace rules.
Creates example scripts for AppArmor, resource limits, firewall rules, and hosts-file blocking.
Provides security tests for sensitive file access, workspace writes, and network reachability.
Outlines monitoring steps for audit logs, network connections, and resource usage.
Produces deployment and security summary documentation for sandbox operations.
limitations: Requires careful human review before running commands with root or administrator privileges.
Example scripts may not match every Linux distribution, container runtime, or Claude Code deployment.
Network allow lists and deny lists must be adapted to each organization.
The skill does not prove compliance without independent testing and audit evidence.

use_cases.title: Prepare a secure coding sandbox
use_cases.description: Define file and network boundaries before allowing agent workflows to run commands.

use_cases.title: Document sandbox controls for review
use_cases.description: Create requirements, threat models, deployment notes, and a security summary for stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Validate isolation in CI environments
use_cases.description: Run controlled tests that check whether sensitive files and blocked domains remain inaccessible.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design file system isolation for a workspace-only sandbox with protected home and system directories.

prompt_templates.title: Configure network isolation
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare network rules and trusted domains.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a network isolation plan with trusted domains, blocked protocols, and validation tests.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my sandbox security deployment plan, identify risky commands, and list manual checks before production use.

output_examples.input: Configure sandbox security for a development workspace.
output: Threat model with file escape, data exfiltration, and resource exhaustion risks.
File policy that permits workspace and temp access while denying sensitive paths.
Validation checklist for sensitive file and network tests.

output_examples.input: Prepare network isolation for agent workflows.
output: Trusted domain list for required services.
Default-deny firewall approach with approved outbound ports.
Tests for allowed and blocked connectivity.

best_practices: Review every privileged command before execution in a real environment.
Start with deny-by-default policies and add only required access.
Run validation tests in an isolated disposable environment before production.
anti_patterns: Running the generated scripts on a workstation without understanding host changes.
Treating example allow lists as complete for every organization.
Using sensitive-file access tests outside a controlled sandbox.

faq.question: What does this skill configure?
faq.answer: It guides file isolation, network restrictions, validation tests, monitoring, and documentation for sandbox security.

faq.question: Does it make changes automatically?
faq.answer: The skill contains commands and scripts. A user or agent must still execute them.

faq.question: Why is human review important?
faq.answer: Some commands modify system directories, firewall rules, and security profiles. These changes can affect the host.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The content is written for Claude Code sandbox workflows and also lists Claude and Codex compatibility.

faq.question: Does it support compliance work?
faq.answer: It can help document controls, but formal compliance requires independent evidence and organizational approval.

faq.question: What should I test first?
faq.answer: Test file access boundaries, network restrictions, resource limits, and rollback procedures in a disposable environment.
